name: Akebu
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Sossoukpe, Jacques 2008, Vitalite ethnolinguistique suivie d'une esquisse phonologique de l'Akebou (cited on Wikipedia Akebu page; not found online)
earlier_scan.note: Tonal language per Wikipedia; the 2008 phonological sketch plausibly covers stress but is unreachable

new_statements.quote: In addition to 11 vowels, Akebu has 24 consonants /p b t d ʈ ɖ c ɟ k g kp gb m n ɲ ŋ f v s z h l y w/ and 3 level tones: low (L), mid (M) and high (H) (Makeeva 2022a). The tone-bearing unit (TBU) in Akebu is the syllable. Contour tones represent sequences of level tones realised on a single TBU and are a result of contextual changes of lexical tones under tonal rules. Akebu has no metrical stress. Four syllable types are possible: V, CV, C1C2V and ŋ. [...] Akebu also manifests the so-called featural foot – a phonotactic unit with a considerable degree of internal phonetic and phonological cohesion in terms of vocalic, consonantal and tonal restrictions (Green 2015; Vydrin 2020).
new_statements.citation: Makeeva, Nadezhda & Natalia Kuznetsova. 2022 [online 2024]. Phonological and acoustic properties of ATR in the vowel system of Akebu (Kwa). Phonology 39(4): 641–678. doi:10.1017/S0952675723000222
new_statements.locator: §1.1 'General features of Akebu phonology', p. 643 (PDF p. 3)
new_statements.reading: no word stress according to the source
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (38 pp., text layer, Cambridge Core OA download, CC-BY notice on p. 641) and re-extracted pp. 1-4 with extracted text. At journal p. 643 (PDF p. 3), sec. 1.1 'General features of Akebu phonology', the passage reads exactly as quoted: '... and 3 level tones: low (L), mid (M) and high (H) (Makeeva 2022a). The tone-bearing unit (TBU) in Akebu is the syllable. Contour tones represent sequences of level tones realised on a single TBU and are a result of contextual changes of lexical tones under tonal rules. Akebu has no metrical stress. Four syllable types are possible: V, CV, C1C2V and ŋ.... Akebu also manifests the so-called featural foot – a phonotactic unit with a considerable degree…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Akebu is a three-level-tone language (L, M, H; syllable = TBU) and, per the principal field phonologist, has no metrical (word) stress; the 'foot' invoked in Akebu descriptions is a phonotactic cohesion domain (vowel/consonant/tone co-occurrence restrictions), not a stress foot.
new_statements.exceptions: None. The only accent-like remark in the literature examined is Wolf 1907 §6 (p. 424), who says that in vowel sequences 'now the first, now the second vowel is accented' and marks it ad hoc; no rule is given and modern descriptions do not take this up.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the word-level prosodic system in general (background section of an instrumental/phonological study based on the first author's 2012 and 2019 fieldwork in Djon village, Akebu prefecture). Makeeva's dedicated phonology papers (2013, 2016, 2022) describe tone and the featural foot and never mention stress, consistent with this explicit statement.
new_statements.identity_note: All modern sources (Makeeva 2013/2016/2022; Makeeva & Kuznetsova 2022; Shluinsky 2020) are based on fieldwork in Djon (Gböndö) and Kotora villages, Akebu prefecture, Togo; Glottolog lists no dialects under akeb1238, so the statement applies at language level. Wolf 1907 'Kögbörikö' is the same language (autonym kə̀gbə̀rə̄kə / kǝkpǝǝ-kǝ).

sources.note: §1.1 'General features of Akebu phonology', p. 643: three level tones (L, M, H), TBU = syllable, contour tones derived; 'Akebu has no metrical stress.' Also describes a 'featural foot' as a purely phonotactic cohesion unit (vowel/consonant/tone co-occurrence restrictions), not a stress foot.

sources.citation: Wolf, Franz. 1907. Grammatik des Kögbörikö (Togo). Anthropos 2: 422–437, 795–820. (archive.org full-volume scanned, item anthroposephemer2190unse)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Lautlehre §6 (p. 424), on vowel sequences only: 'Die Vokale müssen getrennt ausgesprochen werden; doch ist bald der erste, bald der zweite Vokal akzentuiert. Deshalb soll im Folgenden jedesmal der Akzent durch ' bezeichnet werden.' §9: 'Intonation kommt vor' (high/mid/low tone). A footnote (p. 422) says the syllable te in Gbö-te carries the word accent. No general rule for word-stress position.

sources.citation: Makeeva, Nadezhda. 2022. Floating low tone and consonant voicing in Akebu. Language in Africa 3(2): 272–288. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2022-3-2-272-288
sources.note: §3.1 'Tonal system of Akebu' (pp. 277–278): three level tones L/M/H, TBU = syllable, syllable types V, ŋ, CV, C1C2V, mono/di/trisyllabic feet, contour tones from tone rules. No mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Shluinsky, Andrey. 2020. Reduction of noun class suffixes in Akebu. Language in Africa 1(2): 65–88. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-2-65-88
sources.note: §1.2 brief phonology (vowels, tone-bearing nasal, three level tones); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Makeeva, N. V. 2016. Fonotaktika jazyka akebu [Phonotactics of Akebu]. In E. Devjatkina, D. Makhovikov & A. Shluinsky (eds.), Problemy jazyka: sbornik... Četvertoj konferencii-školy, 199–211. Moscow: Kancler. (in Russian; PDF font-shifted, decoded copy saved)
sources.note: Defines the Akebu 'stopa' (foot) as a unit of heightened internal cohesion (restrictions on vowel, consonant and tone combinations; permitted foot tone contours X-L and L-X), plus progressive/regressive vowel harmony. No stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Sossoukpe, Marthe. 2014. Kə lə kə, kə la ŋʊrʊ kəkpəə-kə: guide de transition français–akébou. Lomé: SIL Togo.
sources.note: Literacy primer; Leçon 10 states spoken Akebu distinguishes three tones (haut, moyen, bas) marked selectively with orthographic acute/grave accents. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Makeeva, N. V. 2013. Fonologičeskaja sistema jazyka akebu [Phonological system of Akebu]. In E. Devjatkina, D. Makhovikov & D. Ganenkov (eds.), Problemy jazyka: sbornik... Vtoroj konferencii-školy «Problemy jazyka: vzgljad molodyx učenyx», 262–276. Moscow: Institut jazykoznanija RAN. (in Russian)
sources.note: Full segmental + tonal description (§1.3 Tonal'naja sistema: three level tones + one falling contour toneme, minimal sets). The word 'ударение' does not occur anywhere in the article; silent on stress.
